hypotheses.claim: Traffic signals adapt through local feedback of queue length and vehicle count, adjusting green time to minimize local waiting time
hypotheses.mechanism: Each intersection continuously monitors its own queue length and vehicle count, then adjusts signal timing proportionally to reduce local waiting times without considering downstream effects
evidence: Local traffic sensors can provide real-time queue length data
Some adaptive signal systems use local queue detection
assumptions: Local optimization leads to global optimization
Queue length is the primary determinant of system performance
expected_failure_modes: Braess paradox where local improvements create system-wide congestion
Inability to coordinate platoon movement between intersections
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: Applies the myxomycete principle of local resource optimization to traffic signals without requiring central coordination
hypotheses.testability: Can be tested in simulation by comparing local-only optimization with centralized optimization
hypotheses.falsifier: If implementing local-only optimization results in increased delays at downstream intersections or causes gridlock at network scale

hypotheses.claim: Traffic signals adapt through distributed consensus with neighboring intersections, creating coordinated green waves
hypotheses.mechanism: Each intersection communicates its current state and planned adjustments to adjacent intersections, then reaches consensus on timing that balances local and network-wide objectives
evidence: Distributed consensus algorithms work in other network systems
Coordinated signal systems exist but typically require central planning
assumptions: Intersections can communicate with immediate neighbors
Network-wide objectives can be approximated through local interactions
expected_failure_modes: Inability to reach consensus during rapidly changing conditions
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: Transfers the myxomycete network adaptation principle through distributed consensus rather than purely local decision-making
hypotheses.testability: Can be tested by implementing communication between adjacent intersections and measuring convergence time and solution quality
hypotheses.falsifier: If the communication overhead required for consensus makes real-time adaptation infeasible or if consensus cannot be reached quickly enough to respond to changing conditions

hypotheses.claim: Traffic signals adapt through emergent pattern formation where each intersection follows simple rules based on local conditions, creating system-level optimization
hypotheses.mechanism: Each intersection follows a simple rule set (e.g., increase green time if queue length exceeds threshold, decrease if queue is zero) that, when applied across the network, creates emergent patterns that optimize flow
evidence: Emergent behavior appears in other complex systems
Some traffic signal systems use simple heuristic rules
assumptions: Simple local rules can produce complex global optimization
The network will self-organize into optimal patterns
No explicit communication between intersections is needed
expected_failure_modes: Failure to adapt to non-recurrent congestion patterns
hypotheses.novelty_rationale: Directly transfers the myxomycete emergent computation principle to traffic signal control through simple local rules
hypotheses.testability: Can be tested by implementing simple rule-based signal control and measuring system performance
hypotheses.falsifier: If the simple rules fail to produce optimal flow patterns or create oscillations or instabilities in the network

result.distinguishing_predictions: The local optimization hypothesis would predict maximum improvement at the monitored intersection but potential degradation downstream; the distributed consensus hypothesis would predict coordinated green waves but require communication infrastructure; the emergent pattern hypothesis would predict self-organization but potentially with longer convergence time and oscillatory behavior during transitions. These can be distinguished by measuring: 1) correlation between local improvements and downstream effects, 2) communication requirements and convergence time, and 3) pattern stability and convergence speed under different traffic conditions.
